text:
Mia Chang: quick brain dump 1: per-node package delegation vs central relay for air-gapped customers. operator UX + bandwidth are changing the tradeoffs.
Samir Patel: per-node reduces central bandwidth but increases agent complexity (verification, resume, backoff). more surface area to maintain.
Elaine Gomez: big concern is key material and audit. we should avoid placing signing private keys on hosts. prefer signed artifacts and verifier-only agents.
Mia Chang: idea: verifier-only agents. operator ships a signed manifest + seed catalog. nodes pull chunks, verify signatures locally, then post a signed apply-record token (using the operators published verification key) back to operator for audit. avoids per-node signing keys.
Jonathan Reed: but some sites allow only one outbound egress (single proxy/relay). per-node parallel pulls will swamp that proxy.
Samir Patel: hybrid mode: per-node when network allows; otherwise a relay tier that streams to local subnets, performs dedupe, and enforces rate-limits. relay keeps resume state to avoid re-sending completed chunks.
Mia Chang: rough manifest sketch (plain YAML-like): version: 1; seed: sha256:...; components: - name: runtime; chunk_index: s3://staging/idx/runtime.idx; signature: sig.v1:...
Samir Patel: agent resume semantics: local resume-token per-chunk; agent reports progress; operator can diff tokens to skip already-transferred ranges.
Elaine Gomez: include hooks for KMS/HSM attestation. if site provides a KMS stub, agent fetches an attestation cert and attaches it in the apply-record.
Jonathan Reed: rollout safety model: canary by CIDR + staged activation window. operator should support an "activate-if" predicate and auto-rollback based on healthchecks.
Mia Chang: open questions: how to throttle pulls in relay mode? token-bucket per-relay or per-customer? what metadata is required in apply-record for legal/audit needs? what's canonical apply id for idempotency?
Samir Patel: proposal: throttle at relay with token-bucket tied to relay cert; apply-record fields = [manifest_id, node_id, resume_tokens, verified_signatures, attestation_cert_chain]; canonical apply id = sha256(manifest_id || node_id || activation-window).
Elaine Gomez: key-rotation: manifest signatures must include signer_key_id + rotation_epoch. operator publishes a signed key-rotation manifest with signer history.
Jonathan Reed: failure modes: partial-apply (some components applied, others failed) 1: operator must support staged activation markers and deterministic rollback; agents GC only after operator ACK.
Mia Chang: UX: operator console shows per-node progress and flags nodes stuck on identical chunk (possible cache miss). add a grpc stream for real-time telemetry.
Samir Patel: implementation plan: 1) prototype verifier-only agent with resume-token API + signed apply-records; 2) build relay prototype (dedupe + token-bucket); 3) add key-rotation manifest + minimal attestation; 4) run chaos tests for partial-apply and relay saturation.
deploy-bot: artifact-check: package-proto v0.7.1 signed OK (sha256:abcdef...) :white_check_mark:
Elaine Gomez: security review gate required before relay beta (cache integrity, resume token memory).
Jonathan Reed: I'll draft an RFC for resume-token schema + apply-record fields and include test scenarios. will ask infra for relay perf benchmarks.
Mia Chang: next steps: Jonathan uploads RFC by EOD Tue; Samir stubs token API; Elaine lists compliance fields; Mia sketches console UX. thanks! :wave:
